title: Joint Inference on Direct and Spillover Effects under Sequential Soft Rerandomization
banked_reason: The cited martingale CLT has the reciprocal Lindeberg cutoff epsilon*V_T^(-1/2); a Rademacher triangular array satisfies its premises but not its Gaussian conclusion.
gap_reasons: li_zhao_martingale_clt is false as stated, due to a reciprocal threshold error
The correct cutoff is epsilon*sqrt(V_T), which changes the frozen .tex claim
proof_attempt_summary: A reusable martingale-array CLT was built, reviewed, promoted, and independently axiom-audited. Instantiating it exposed that the frozen Li--Zhao lemma uses the reciprocal Lindeberg cutoff epsilon/sqrt(V_T): a one-increment Rademacher array satisfies the displayed premises while its normalized sum stays Rademacher. The headline CLT remains retryable after correcting the source cutoff and can use the already-promoted fourth-moment corollary directly.
tldr: Predictable soft rerandomization balances lagged group outcomes while preserving the fixed sustained direct-and-spillover target.  The bounded lag-one partial-interference class contains only structural and design-regularity conditions.  On this class, complement symmetry gives exact first-order propensities, score splitting isolates the balanced-sign component, and singular-support Gaussian transport is uniform without covariance-limit assumptions.  Many-block joint inference separately requires rerandomization covariance stabilization and a positive-definite limit, whereas the projection identity \(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{CR}}-(1-v_{\eta,\kappa})P\) is a distinct \(G\to\infty\) result requiring the complete-randomization, rerandomization, and projection stabilizations but not positive definiteness.  Logged pair probabilities and a positive-semidefinite completion yield an observable conservative \(2\)-by-\(2\) studentizer and simultaneous Wald coverage.
gap: Existing papers separately cover static spillover-and-carryover design, sequential balance, general adaptive IPW martingales, and static rerandomization projection geometry. None supplies the history-uniform soft-tilt quadratic-moment transport that joins these layers under fixed-half group saturations and fixed-count within-group assignment.
fill: The project derives exact unbiasedness, a two-stage martingale/combinatorial central limit theorem, an observable PSD-conservative matrix studentizer, simultaneous coverage, and an explicit projection covariance gain, with the singular weighted Gaussian approximation exposed as the first open theorem step.
